ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the intersection point of the lines $y=-x+a$ and $y=x+b$ has an abscissa of $-2$, and the abscissas of the points where the two lines intersect with the $x$ axis are $-1$ and $-3$, respectively. What is the solution set of the inequality $-x+a>x+b>0$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ the intersection point of the line $y = -x + a$ and $y = x + b$ has an x-coordinate of $-2$, and the x-intercepts of the two lines are $-1$ and $-3$ respectively, \\
$\therefore$ the solution set for the inequality in $x$, $-x + a > x + b > 0$, is the range of $x$ values for which the line $y = -x + a$ is above the line $y = x + b$, that is, $-3 < x < -2$.\\
Thus, the answer is: $\boxed{-3 < x < -2}$.
